message.content:
### Rough Estimate of Annual Electricity Use for a 2,000 sq ft Home

| Metric | Typical Value (US) | How It’s Calculated |
|--------|--------------------|---------------------|
| **Annual kWh per square foot** | 4–6 kWh/sq ft | Based on U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) data for average residential consumption. |
| **Estimated annual consumption** | **≈ 10 000–12 000 kWh** | 2,000 sq ft × 5 kWh/sq ft (mid‑point) |
| **Monthly average** | **≈ 833–1 000 kWh** | 10 000–12 000 kWh ÷ 12 months |
| **Daily average** | **≈ 28–33 kWh/day** | 10 000–12 000 kWh ÷ 365 days |

> **Bottom line:** A 2,000 sq ft house in the U.S. typically uses **about 10–12 kWh per square foot per year**, which translates to roughly **10,000–12,000 kWh per year** (≈ 833–1,000 kWh per month).

---

## Why the Numbers Vary

| Factor | Effect on Consumption |
|--------|-----------------------|
| **Climate** | Hot climates → more cooling; cold climates → more heating. |
| **Insulation & windows** | Better insulation reduces heating/cooling load. |
| **Appliances & electronics** | High‑efficiency appliances lower usage; many devices or a home office increase it. |
| **Occupancy** | More occupants → more lights, water heaters, etc. |
| **Behavior** | Usage patterns (e.g., leaving lights on, thermostat settings). |

If you’re in a particularly hot or cold region, or if you have a lot of electric heat or a large HVAC system, your consumption could be on the higher end of the range. Conversely, a well‑insulated, energy‑efficient home with smart thermostats and LED lighting could be on the lower end.

---
